chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
Blood is on my garment while I am in salat (prayer).

He said: “If you see it and you are wearing another garment besides it, then cast it off and pray in the other one. If you do not have another garment on you, then continue in your salat (prayer), and there is no repetition upon you so long as it does not exceed the measure of a dirham. If it is less than a dirham, then it is nothing, whether you saw it or did not see it. And if you had seen it and it was more than the measure of a dirham, then you neglected washing it and prayed in it many prayers, then repeat what you prayed in it. And that is not in the same rank as semen or urine.”
Then he عليه السلام mentioned semen, and was strict concerning it, and made it more severe than urine.

Then he عليه السلام said: “If you see semen before or after, then repetition is upon you—the repetition of the salat (prayer). And if you examined your garment and did not find it, and you prayed in it, then there is no repetition upon you. And likewise urine.”

key_terms.إِعَادَةَ: repetition of the prayer due to impurity-related invalidation
key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment on which impurity may be present during salat (prayer)
key_terms.الدَّمُ: blood as an impurity discussed in relation to the validity of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْبَوْلِ: urine, cited here in comparison with blood and semen
key_terms.الْمَنِيَّ: semen, treated here as a more severe impurity than blood and urine
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: a measure used here as the legal threshold for the amount of blood
key_terms.غَسْلَهُ: washing the impurity from the garment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying with blood, semen, or urine on one’s garment?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning blood, semen, and urine on a garment during salat (prayer). It explains when a garment should be removed, when salat may be continued without repetition, and when previous prayers must be repeated, distinguishing the ruling of blood from the stricter ruling of semen and also addressing urine.
